subject: Hosted latency check-in: probing p95/p99 and streaming constraints
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Gaunt <alex.gaunt@veridianhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted latency check-in: probing p95/p99 and streaming constraints

Alex — great to meet earlier. Quick post-call recap so we have a shared starting point and concrete next steps for the performance validation. TL;DR: we believe hosted can meet your p95/p99 E2E targets with a short PoC; below are the assumptions we want to validate.

What we discussed (assumptions to confirm)
- Target E2E (client->app->Redwood->model->client) goals: p95 <= 120ms, p99 <= 350ms for text generation at 16 token responses under your steady-state profile.
- Streaming behavior: you need sub-100ms first-token for streaming enablement at concurrency up to 40 active streams.
- Throughput: baseline ~120 qps peak, 60 sustained; bursts to 300 qps for short windows.
- KV/prefix cache: your traffic contains many repeated prefixes (helpful). We proposed enabling prefix caching to reduce per-token work for repeated prompts.
- Fallbacks: when capacity constrained we can route to a slightly lower-cost quantized variant with expected p95 degradation ~+40ms p99 +120ms (to be measured).

Requested artifacts / immediate asks from Veridian
- A sample traffic strip (1k requests) with timestamps, avg prompt length, and streaming vs non-streaming indicator.
- Your current provider's p95/p99 snapshots for the same window (attachment you mentioned).

Next steps (agreed on call)
1) You drop a small traffic sample to the shared Drive (see link).
2) We produce a lightweight PoC harness and run a 2-hour soak at your steady-state profile and one 30-minute burst window.
3) We share a result deck with per-route p50/p95/p99 and token-level breakdown; if we hit thresholds we discuss commercial terms/commitment sizing.

I've attached the initial SLO matrix and a short PoC test plan. Ben & Laura — can you own the PoC runbook and confirm resource slots for next week?

Thanks,

Jasmine Liu
Enterprise Lead, Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: redwood-slo-matrix-20270405.xlsx (SLO/assumption workbook), poc-test-plan.txt (PoC steps)
From: Alex Gaunt <alex.gaunt@veridianhealth.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@veridianhealth.com
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 17:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted latency check-in: probing p95/p99 and streaming constraints

Thanks Jasmine — useful recap. Couple clarifications from our side before we drop the sample: 

1) The p95/p99 targets you listed are for full E2E including TLS termination at our edge and app-layer processing, right? We need to be explicit: our app adds ~20-30ms on average.
2) For streaming, first-token is critical (we measure from HTTP upgrade to first byte). Is the sub-100ms you mentioned inclusive of network RTT from our primary region in us-west-2?

We have exported a 2-hour window of production traffic and attached our incumbent snapshot (veridian-incumbent-latency-snapshot.pdf). We'll upload the lightweight strip (anonymized) to the Drive link by EOD tomorrow.

If you can, please include the exact measurement points your PoC will capture — we want apples-to-apples comparisons.

Alex
Alex Gaunt
Senior Engineering Manager, Veridian Health
alex.gaunt@veridianhealth.com

Attachment: veridian-incumbent-latency-snapshot.pdf
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 06 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted latency check-in: probing p95/p99 and streaming constraints

Looping in internal owners and next actions.

Laura — can you own the PoC harness (k6 script + streaming client) and provision a short-lived dedicated pool in our staging-hosted cluster? I'll coordinate capacity and priority with infra.

Checklist I'm using for the run:
- Measurement points: client send timestamp, server receipt, first-token emit, final token emit.
- Network baseline: synthetic RTTs from our hosted region to us-west-2 (we'll capture ICMP/TCP handshakes as baseline).
- Concurrency model: steady 60 qps with 40 concurrent streaming channels; burst test to 300 qps for 30 mins.
- Variant comparison: run with quantized variant and standard fp16 variant back-to-back.

Also: we should include a tiny synthetic test that reproduces your worst-case prompt length (you said ~420 tokens) so we see tail behavior.

Ben
Ben Carter
Principal Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

On Mon, Apr 5, 2027 at 15:05 Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Alex — great to meet earlier. Quick post-call recap so we have a shared starting point...
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Gaunt <alex.gaunt@veridianhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, procurement@veridianhealth.com
Date: Wed, 07 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted latency check-in: probing p95/p99 and streaming constraints

Alex — thanks for the snapshot. Confirming a couple of points inline:
- Yes, our p95/p99 references are full E2E (including TLS and app-layer). We'll capture the same timestamps you outlined.
- The sub-100ms first-token expectation assumes <40ms network RTT; if your RTT is larger we'll add that delta to expectations and call out the numbers in the result deck.

I've scheduled the PoC kickoff for next Wednesday, Apr 14 at 10:00am PT — 30 minute sync to review harness and success criteria. Laura, Ben — please lock resources and post the run results to the Drive link inside the PoC folder. Alex / procurement — once we get successful latency acceptance we can switch to term discussions; I'll drop a proposed SOW template after the run.

Best,

Jasmine
